text:
There is so much love in my soul that no room remains
not even the narrowest corner for hate.
Where do you want me to put the resentments
that your vilenesses might engender?


I am not impassive: I feel everything,
I suffer everything… But like the child
whom they make cry, as soon as he sees
a toy before his eyes
he consoles himself, smiles,
and stretches his eager hands
toward it without remembering the pain,
so I, before the divine panorama
of my idea, before the ineffable
of my infinite love,
feel neither the evil pinprick
nor the cruel sharp
irony, nor hear the sarcastic
laughter. I forget everything,
because I am only heart, only eyes
nothing more, to lean from the window
and watch the ineffable Dream pass,
dressed in violet,
and with all the light of morning
in his divine eyes, in the quiet
clarity of the fountain…

translation.title: So Much Love
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the child-and-toy comparison and the violet-clad Dream at the fountain. The source compresses “todo…Pero” without a following space; the English restores the sentence spacing.
